discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI Innsbruck, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: J. Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and Cirac turned Feynman's vision of quantum simulation into a concrete programme: their 1998 proposal (with Jaksch, Bruder and Gardiner) showed that cold atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable interactions, and their broader theory gave controllable, engineered quantum matter a common language. Bloch's 2002 observation of the superfluid-Mott insulator transition confirmed this spectacularly and opened a field: Fermi-Hubbard antiferromagnetism, many-body localisation, artificial gauge fields and topological bands, and single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy. Optical-lattice simulators now address questions in condensed matter, high-energy lattice gauge theories and quantum information that classical computation cannot. This is a rare case of simple, predictive theory adopted as an experimental working tool across communities, uniting quantum optics and many-body physics and laying foundations of today's quantum technologies.
